title: AI found 948 Linux root bugs
youtube_title: OpenAI's AI found 948 Linux root exploits in one run
description:
OpenAI says an automated AI pipeline found 948 distinct Linux kernel privilege-escalation flaws in a single run, for about $1.2M in API credits. Caveats: local access required, human-reviewed, most fixes still in the reporting pipeline.

Sources:

https://interestingengineering.com/ai-robotics/openai-agents-linux-kernel-vulnerabilities-exploits
https://dev.to/yehechuhai/948-linux-root-exploits-in-one-run-what-openais-kernel-pipeline-actually-proves-and-what-it-47a
story_title: OpenAI's AI pipeline finds 948 Linux kernel privilege-escalation flaws in one run

scenes.voiceover: OpenAI says its AI just found nine hundred forty-eight ways to get root access on Linux. In a single run.
Its agents scanned about two point eight million lines of the Linux kernel. That's roughly seven percent of it.
In twelve hours they flagged over two thousand possible bugs, then rebuilt one thousand seven hundred twenty-four in test machines to prove they were real.
The bill? About one point two million dollars in API credits. Roughly twelve hundred seventy-nine dollars per unique flaw.
Back in July, an earlier model found one hundred sixty-six, for less than half the cost.
Before you panic: these need local access to a machine, humans reviewed the findings before reporting, and only sixty-one were patched upstream when the scan ended.
Finding bugs just got cheap. Fixing them is the new bottleneck. Follow for daily AI news, fact-checked.

claims.final_wording: OpenAI says its AI pipeline found 948 distinct Linux kernel local privilege-escalation (root) vulnerabilities in a single run in mid-October 2026, published Nov 4.

evidence.supports: 948 unique LPE vulnerabilities; reported Nov 4; run in mid-October
948 distinct LPE vulnerabilities after variant analysis

claims.note: Self-reported by OpenAI; attribute on air.

claims.final_wording: The agents audited about 2.8 million lines, roughly 7% of the Linux kernel.
Analysts produced 2,308 candidate findings in 12 hours; 1,724 were reproduced in isolated virtual machines.

evidence.supports: 1,724 validated by reproduction in isolated VMs

claims.final_wording: The run cost about $1.21 million in API credits, roughly $1,279 per unique vulnerability (an upper bound).
A July 2026 run with an earlier model found 166 unique LPE vulnerabilities for $513,690.
At the end of the scan 61 were patched upstream and 43 had staging patches; the rest were still being reported.
The flaws are local privilege escalations (attacker needs local access), and human researchers reviewed findings before reporting.
